title: SQLite: setup, CLI, and shell commands

questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “SQLite: setup, CLI, and shell commands”?
options: Start with a small, readable SELECT query; connect it to an application only after you understand its result.
The query returns Ada and 42 in two columns.
SQLite often runs inside the application; MySQL and PostgreSQL commonly run as separate server processes.
The first commands run in the SQLite shell; PRAGMA and SELECT are SQL statements sent to the database.
questions.answer: The first commands run in the SQLite shell; PRAGMA and SELECT are SQL statements sent to the database.
questions.explanation:
The first commands run in the SQLite shell; PRAGMA and SELECT are SQL statements sent to the database.
Why: SQLite is useful for learning SQL and storing local data without installing a separate server. `sqlite3 school.db` opens or creates a file in the terminal. `.tables` lists tables and `.schema students` shows a table definition; `.mode column` and `.headers on` make results readable; `.read setup.sql` runs a SQL file; `.backup copy.db` creates a backup; `.quit` exits. Dot-prefixed commands belong to the SQLite shell, not standard SQL. The SQL statement `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;` enables foreign-key checks for the current connection. In Python, `sqlite3.connect` opens the database and parameterized `execute` calls run queries.
